title: METR Time Horizons and External Capability Evaluation

questions.question: Which input transformation does fit use for task duration?
options: The raw duration in seconds
The square root of duration
log(t), so the logistic curve is fit over task time on a log scale
A binary short/long flag
questions.explanation: fit computes sigmoid(w * log(t) + b), matching the synthetic generator's log-duration model.

questions.question: For a fitted slope w and intercept b, how does horizon_at(w, b, 0.5) find the 50% time?
options: It returns exp(b*w)
It always returns the synthetic true_h value
It returns logit(.5) without exponentiating
It returns exp((0 - b) / w), because logit(.5)=0
questions.explanation: The inverse logistic uses log(t)=(logit(p)-b)/w; at p=.5 the logit is zero, so the function exponentiates -b/w.

questions.question: What does inject_gaming(tasks, 0.4) do to eligible examples?
options: It flips some failures to successes, which can bias the fitted observed horizon upward
It flips successes to failures at every duration
It changes every task duration to 0.4 hours
It changes the model's slope without refitting
questions.explanation: For each failed task, the function uses random.random() < gaming_rate to turn it into a success; fit then sees an easier evaluation context.

questions.question: Why does sigmoid return exactly 1.0 for x > 50 and 0.0 for x < -50?
options: Those values are sampled randomly
The explicit saturation branches avoid extreme exponential calculations
The fitted slope is always one
horizon_at clamps the probability after fitting
questions.explanation: sigmoid has explicit numerical guard branches at ±50 before evaluating exp(-x), making extreme logits stable.

questions.question: How are the synthetic task durations in synth_tasks distributed?
options: Uniformly between 0 and 1 hour
All exactly 14 hours
Log-uniformly over about 0.05 to 48 hours, via a uniform draw in log space
Only at the 10%, 50%, and 90% horizons
questions.explanation: The generator draws uniform random values between log(.05) and log(48), then exponentiates them, producing log-spread task times.

questions.question: What does fit return after its gradient-descent loop?
options: The three horizon values directly
A list of all task labels
The gaming rate and the true horizon
The fitted logistic slope w and intercept b
questions.explanation: fit updates w and b using the p-y gradients over log(t) and returns that pair; horizon_at converts it to 10%, 50%, or 90% times.
